text: "The Night Market" is the fourth episode of the fourth season of the American mockumentary comedy horror series What We Do in the Shadows, set in Staten Island, New York City, and serves as the 34th overall episode of the series. It was written by co-producer William Meny and executive producer Paul Simms, and directed by co-executive producer Yana Gorskaya. FX aired the episode on July 26, 2022. The series follows three vampires—Nandor, Laszlo, and Nadja—alongside Colin Robinson, an energy vampire, and Guillermo, Nandor's familiar. In this episode, the vampires visit a secret night market accessible via a subway train, a marketplace used by various supernatural creatures. Laszlo introduces Baby Colin (Mark Proksch) to fairies, while Nandor introduces Guillermo to the "familiar fight," a combat event where vampires bring their familiars to fight to death. When Guillermo is revealed as a familiar, the ringmaster asks him to fight, which Nandor allows because he is being booed for not participating. Guillermo easily defeats other familiars and is awarded dried-up dog food, but is still booed for not harming them. He is then challenged to fight the champion vampire, Gorgo the Murderer, but since fighting would expose his ancestry, Nandor takes Gorgo's place and fights Guillermo. Their battle spreads across the stage, resulting in several creature deaths. When Guillermo has the chance to stake Nandor, he suggests faking Gorgo's death, and Nandor pretends to snap Guillermo's neck, allowing them to escape. Nadja returns to the nightclub and exposes Xerxes, the wraith union leader, to water lily of the Nile, a narcotic for wraiths, attempting to persuade him to abandon his demands. Xerxes agrees in exchange for the narcotic, but the other wraiths discover this and kill him. Nadja reluctantly accepts their terms, and the wraiths return to work. Back home, Baby Colin asks Laszlo to read him a "real stuff" book instead of fairytales, and Laszlo reads him In Cold Blood. In June 2022, FX confirmed the episode's title, writers, and director. In its original American broadcast, "The Night Market" was seen by an estimated 0.339 million household viewers with a 0.11 ratings share among adults aged 18–49, representing a 44% increase from the previous episode, which was watched by 0.234 million household viewers with a 0.15 ratings share in the same demographic. The episode received positive reviews from critics, with William Hughes of The A.V. Club giving it a "B" and praising the humor and the Guillermo-Nandor fight as a resolution to prior "Who would win in a fight?" questions. Katie Rife of Vulture gave it a 4-star rating, highlighting the episode's fantastical elements and the stinky subway performer. Tony Sokol of Den of Geek awarded it 4 stars, calling it a "bargain at any price" and noting the variety of supernatural creatures. Melody McCune of Telltale TV gave it a 4.5-star rating, praising the action, scale, and performances, especially Nandermo and Nadja's haggling. Alejandra Bodden of Bleeding Cool gave it a 9 out of 10, stating it effectively showcases the vampires' care for one another and is a standout episode in the series' growing list of excellence.
